reactions.kinetics_basis: Stored-gas water exchange uses signed net liquid-to-vapor rate from the shared chemical potential; negative evaporation extent increments mean condensation. Bounded reverse kinetics are proportional to existing liquid. Swept-gas host retains its prior one-way law.
Stored-gas mode uses local chemical affinity including surface energy, with explicit oxygen-order factor; swept mode retains conservative carrier bounds.

Finite-gas mode permits signed net calcite-to-lime/CO2 extent. Positive affinity allows reverse consumption of local lime and CO2 with the same thermodynamic ledger; zero reverse factor and historical swept mode remain irreversible.
Stored-gas mode uses local chemical affinity including surface energy, with explicit oxygen-order factor; swept mode retains conservative carrier bounds.
Stored-gas mode uses local chemical affinity including surface energy, with explicit oxygen-order factor; swept mode retains conservative carrier bounds.
Lumped oxygen-independent first-order carbonization competes for the same organic inventory as oxidation; affinity-limited. Produced char can subsequently oxidize.

Signed portlandite->lime+vapor; negative extent is hydration. Both branches use same full affinity, available solid donor and a positive assumed Arrhenius mobility. Reverse scales with steam activity. No separate reaction heat or empirical equilibrium-pressure law.
